summary.en: A school roof collapsed in Peshawar, killing dozens of children and a teacher, prompting families to demand justice and prompting authorities to order school inspections. The Pakistani government has imposed emergency rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa amid rising tension, while the Taliban and Russia are drawing closer, heightening regional strain. An emergency border response is underway in Afghanistan, as detailed in a ReliefWeb report covering late September to early October 2026. The conflict in the region produced 1,794 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Et skoletak i Peshawar kollapset, og drepte dusinvis av barn og en lærer, noe som førte til at familiene krevde rettferdighet og myndighetene beordret skoleinspeksjoner. Den pakistanske regjeringen har innført unntakstilstand i Khyber Pakhtunkhwa på grunn av økende spenning, mens Taliban og Russland kommer nærmere hverandre, noe som øker den regionale belastningen. En nødrespons ved grensen er i gang i Afghanistan, som beskrevet i en ReliefWeb-rapport som dekker slutten av september til begynnelsen av oktober 2026. Konflikten i regionen førte til 1 794 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
background.extract: Since 2004, an insurgency has been fought in the Pakistani province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa by Islamist militant groups such as the Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), Jundallah, Lashkar-e-Islam (LeI), the Tehreek-e-Nafaz-e-Shariat-e-Mohammadi (TNSM), Al-Qaeda, and their Central Asian allies such as the Islamic State – Khorasan Province (ISKP), Islamic Movement of Uzbekistan, East Turkistan Movement, Jamaat-ul-Ahrar, Ittihad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan, and elements of organised crime. Before being transformed into an insurgency in 2017, the conflict was a war.
